 Everything New in iOS 27.3 Beta 2
 Monday November 16, 2026 4:15 pm PST by Juli Clover Apple released the second beta of iOS 27.3 today, and like the first beta , it has several major new features. There are improvements to the iPhone Duo , tweaks to apps, new Siri features, and more.
 iPhone Duo Face Unlock
 Apple added a new option to quickly unlock the iPhone Duo using the front-facing camera. The option is only available when the ‌iPhone Duo‌ is closed, and it can only be used on the Lock Screen.
Authenticating with Touch ID is required for Apple Pay purchases and for accessing passwords and logins. Unlocking with the camera requires recent ‌Touch ID‌ or passcode authentication, and ‌Touch ID‌ is required again after about 45 minutes of inactivity.
 Unlocking with the front-facing camera does not work when the ‌iPhone Duo‌ is open, presumably because the under-display camera is not high enough quality. The face unlock feature can be turned on in the Settings app under ‌Touch ID‌ and Passcode.
 iPhone Duo Lock When Closed
 Apple added an option to lock the ‌iPhone Duo‌ when it's closed instead of transferring content to the front display.
Close to Lock can be turned on in the Display and Brightness section of the Settings app.
 Siri AI
 There's a new "Ask About Page" feature for ‌Siri‌ AI that lets ‌Siri‌ see the entire content of a webpage, even if it's not currently in view on the screen.
 ‌Siri‌ AI can also now access Health data when given permission, and control over smart home products has improved.
 Apple Intelligence and Siri AI Usage Limits
 iOS 27.3 introduces the Apple Intelligence usage limits cxdApple has been warning about for months. ‌Siri‌ AI and ‌Apple Intelligence‌ features that use server-side processing will now have daily usage limits on a per-device basis.
 Extra access is tied to 200GB and higher iCloud + plans. The 200GB plan gives up to 2x usage, the 2TB plan is up to 5x, the 6TB plan is up to 10x, and the 12TB plan is up to 20x.
 Limits apply to complex ‌Siri‌ AI requests that involve multiple steps, image generation and editing tools, AI workflows and automations in Shortcuts, and third-party apps that use Apple Foundation Models in Private Cloud Compute. More information can be found in our article on the new limits .
 Calendar
 The Calendar app has an updated layout with the options for searching and adding an event moved to the bottom of the app. The "Today" button that takes you to the current date has also been updated to show the date.
 Apple TV App Podcasts
 Video podcast episodes are now available in the Apple TV app. Only video podcasts that are free will show up in the ‌Apple TV‌ app.
 Apple News+ Puzzles
 Apple News + Puzzles are expanding to Australian, UK, and French-Canadian ‌Apple News‌+ subscribers.
 Subscribers in Australia get access to a daily quick crossword, crossword mini, Sudoku, Quartiles, and Emoji Game. UK subscribers get the daily quick crossword, crossword mini, and Sudoku, while French-Canadian subscribers can play Quartiles and Emoji Game.
 Weather App
 There are 10 new weather condition symbols in the Weather app, but Apple doesn't appear to be using them yet.
 The Weather app gets 10 new weather-condition symbols in iOS 27.3 beta 2. https://t.co/1c5W4n5gKn
— pdfu (@itspdfu) November 16, 2026 
 Home App
 The Home app has an "Unrecognized People" section that limits how guests can use Safari and ‌Siri‌ on Apple home devices.
 Apple Music
 There's code in Apple Music for an album release countdown , but it doesn't appear to be active yet.

iPhone Duo face unlock working well. Great addition.
 Finally the basic photo unlock from nearly all windows and android devices, that was described as not safe enough and cheap by Apple over all these years… now added to the most expensive smartphone of their lineup 😅😅😅 Score: 15 Votes ( Like | Disagree ) ScreenSavers 21 hours ago at 04:25 pm iPhone Duo face unlock working well. Great addition. Score: 9 Votes ( Like | Disagree ) T Tagbert 19 hours ago at 05:41 pm 
Finally the basic photo unlock from nearly all windows and android devices, that was described as not safe enough and cheap by Apple over all these years… now added to the most expensive smartphone of their lineup 😅😅😅
 It is clearly a compromise feature since FaceID can’t go on this model. Face unlock only works after you have authenticated with touchID or passcode and then it just extends the session for 45 minutes before you need to authenticate again. It looks like a nice convenience feature for a device with so many screens and no FaceID. The lower security of a 2D facial scan should be a reasonable compromise of security over convenience and is optional. 
i wonder if they are doing a dynamic scan with multiple snaps to get a sense of your face’s 3D shape to make sure it isn’t a photo. A little movement should show enough parallax to confirm that you are a 3D person and not a 2D print. Score: 5 Votes ( Like | Disagree ) fj_doebz 19 hours ago at 06:04 pm So why not bring face unlock to iPad mini and Air? Score: 4 Votes ( Like | Disagree ) U Unregistered 4U 19 hours ago at 05:51 pm Someone wrote “Good to see Apple adapting quickly to real-world feedback.” People seriously think Apple put this together in the last month? And that it wasn’t simply on their roadmap (along with lots of other things yet to be released)? I mean, I’m guessing Apple’s fine with folks thinking they “listened and responded to feedback”, but there’s no way this wasn’t an intended feature all along.
If a leaker doesn’t mention it, it doesn’t mean that it was never there and Apple just decided to work on it in the last few weeks. It’s because the person one may THINK is a leaker, isn’t. None of those in the list of folks who claim to be “in the know” were aware of this fairly big change coming in this release (but will confidently talk about things next year which still “might not happen”. ;) I think we’ll find that even the choice of the camera hardware, something confirmed, purchased and made available to Apple’s manufacturers awhile ago helped to make this happen.
